question: What is the main duty of a nurse when it comes to hospital equipment?

options.A: Purchasing new devices from international vendors
options.B: Repairing major electrical faults on wards
options.C: Ensuring daily handling and functional readiness

explanation: You've got this! Nurses handle equipment daily and make sure everything is clean, working, and ready to keep patients safe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: An infusion pump is an example of which type of hospital equipment?
explanation: Nice one! Therapeutic devices like infusion pumps actively deliver treatments, such as medications and fluids, directly to your patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: When should portable clinical items be returned to their proper storage spot?

options.C: At the end of the month

explanation: Always return items right away! It saves precious time when another nurse urgently needs them during an emergency. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is it so important to clean equipment right after you use it?

options.A: It automatically recalibrates electronic digital sensors
options.B: It removes the need for final sterilization
options.C: It charges the internal batteries of portable devices
options.D: It prevents organic matter from hardening on sensitive surfaces

explanation: Spot on. Washing things right away stops body fluids from drying up and sticking hard, making the next steps much easier! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the final step in processing contaminated surgical instruments?
explanation: You nailed it! Sterilization is the final knockout punch that destroys all germs and spores, making tools completely safe for surgery. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which process uses soap and water to get rid of visible dirt and organic mess?
explanation: Think of cleaning as the essential first wash. It physically removes the visible dirt before you move on to disinfection or sterilization. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: How should you store rubber goods like tubing so they don't spoil quickly?

options.A: Packed inside sealed plastic bags in direct sunlight
options.B: Tightly coiled in a warm, sunny room
options.C: Flat or hanging loosely without kinks
options.D: Folded into sharp creases inside metal drawers

explanation: Keep rubber happy by storing it flat or hanging loose! Avoiding sharp bends and hot spots stops it from cracking and losing its stretch. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for running regular inventory checks on your ward?

options.A: Training junior staff on minor equipment repairs
options.B: Testing the electrical voltage of wall sockets
options.C: Removing the need for biomedical engineering checks
options.D: Preventing hoarding and ensuring equitable distribution

explanation: Inventory checks keep things fair! They help track hospital property so no single room hoards supplies that other patients urgently need. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is your very first step when you notice a piece of equipment is broken?

options.A: Throw it directly into the general waste bin
options.B: Leave it on the trolley for the next shift
options.C: Withdraw the item from service and tag it
options.D: Attempt to solder the loose internal wires

explanation: Safety first! Always pull a faulty item out of action and slap a warning tag on it so nobody accidentally uses it on a patient. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why shouldn't nurses try quick DIY fixes on broken ward electronics?

options.A: It invalidates the manufacturer warranty on rubber goods
options.B: It violates hospital cleaning and sterilization protocols
options.C: It slows down the routine morning inventory stock count
options.D: It introduces severe safety risks and potential electrical hazards

explanation: Leave electronics to the pros! Quick DIY fixes can cause shocks, start fires, or make the machine fail when someone's life depends on it. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)
